paper.quote: embedding unit 116 receives horizontal-velocity weights 2.25, 2.37, and 1.73 from the body and wheels
paper.say: The model says the trained network acts like a speed-sensitive throttle, choosing between driving and coasting. As evidence it points to one first-layer unit that reads the sideways speed of the car's body and both wheels.

check.note: All three values match, and they are the three largest weights into unit 116. One unit alone does not show how the whole network uses speed.

paper.quote: Head rows 6 and 114 strongly oppose “off” and “drive +1.”
paper.say: The model says two units just before the output push the choice between coasting and driving in opposite directions.

check.note: Both rows have opposite signs on these two moves. Ranked by the size of that difference across all 128 rows, they are number 1 and number 2.

paper.quote: the car approaches the ramp, loses its momentum, then alternates throttle and coasting without advancing
paper.say: The model read the recorded failed episode. It says the car reaches the ramp, runs out of speed, and then flips between driving and coasting while going nowhere.

check.note: In the recorded episode the body stays at x = 2.00 to 2.01 from step 32 to step 255, while the action flips between off and drive left. The cause of the lost speed cannot be read from this table.

paper.say: The model says the network almost never picks reverse.

check.note: Reverse has probability 0.00 in all 17 listed rows of the one recorded episode.

paper.quote: It collects distance-shaping reward but never makes the launch needed to clear red.
paper.say: The model says the car earns a small reward for getting closer to the blue box, yet never makes the jump it needs to clear the red strip.

check.note: The paper's result for this network is 0 successes in 256 episodes, all timeouts, with mean return 0.152.

paper.quote: I will retain the learned network except for a small isolated control path.
paper.say: The model's plan is to keep the trained network and add one small separate circuit to handle what fails.

check.note: The circuit uses 19 of the 768 hidden units, and 6,073 of 171,664 weights change (3.5%). No wire joins these units to the trained units. Those 19 units are taken away from the trained network.

paper.quote: That path supplies a reverse run-up and a committed leftward launch, then releases control once green has cleared red.
paper.say: The model says the circuit does three things in order. It backs the car up, drives hard to the left, and hands control back once the green wheel has cleared the red strip.

check.note: The paper reports success in 1,024 of 1,024 test episodes, 73 steps each. The recorded episode shows these three phases.

paper.quote: The override backs right from rest, switches to leftward drive around body x = 3.8
paper.say: The model says the car starts by reversing to the right. When its body reaches about x = 3.8, the circuit switches to driving left.

check.note: The switch sits at 304 / 80 = 3.8 exactly. In the recorded episode the body is at x = 3.85 at step 16 and already driving left, and it coasts on to x = 4.18.

paper.quote: A slow approach near the ramp instead triggers another run-up.
paper.say: The model says that if the car comes toward the ramp too slowly, the circuit makes it back up and try again.

check.note: This holds for x below 2.5 and leftward speed under 1.5. Astra does not mention a gap: for x between 2.5 and 3.1 at that speed, the circuit switches off and the trained network decides.

paper.quote: Position and velocity distinguish backing from returning without recurrent memory.
paper.say: The network has no memory of earlier steps. The model says position and speed together are enough to tell whether the car is still backing up or already coming back.

check.note: At x = 3.5 the circuit reverses when the speed is +1 and drives left when it is −3. The map below shows the full rule.

paper.quote: Large logit margins make the decisive actions nearly deterministic despite sampling.
paper.say: The game picks each move at random, weighted by the network's scores. The model says the circuit's scores are so far apart that the intended move is chosen nearly every time.

check.note: The winning score leads by about 600. All trained units together could shift a score by at most about 33, so they cannot overturn it.

paper.quote: Once green’s centre passes x = 0.95—its right edge is then left of red—the override switches off.
paper.say: The model says that once the centre of the green wheel passes x = 0.95, the whole wheel is clear of the red strip, so the circuit turns itself off.

check.note: The switch sits at 76 / 80 = 0.95 exactly. The wheel's radius is 0.22, so its right edge is at 1.17, and the red strip starts at 1.18.

paper.quote: The bias offsets cancel its inactive outputs, restoring the remaining learned policy.
paper.say: The model says it added fixed constants so that a switched-off circuit adds nothing to the move scores. The rest of the trained network then drives.

check.note: When off, the circuit leaves the three scores at 0.03, 0.05 and −0.19, the trained network's original constants.
